name: align_lna_qm
description: Differential common-source LNA core (M4/M13) with resistively-loaded/trimmed outputs (a 10-resistor VDD-to-OUTP/OUTN ladder network) and multiple VMAIN-node decoupling caps. From ALIGN's CircuitsDatabase example library (real, previously-taped-out mmWave phased-array front-end block, library name 'PhasedArray_WB_copy').

source.process: Not specified in the excerpt (ALIGN's example decks are process-anonymised for the public repo); device models 'nmos', 'rppolywo_rf', 'res', 'cap', 'ind' are generic placeholders, not tied to a named PDK here.
source.format_as_retrieved: Spectre-syntax subckt with AnalogGenie-like 'Dev (pin list) type' device lines (see source/LNA_TB.scs); a companion hierarchical HSPICE-style top view (source/LNA_QM.sp) exists in the same folder but references PDK subcircuits ('resistor','mimcap','nmos','ind') with no local definitions, so it was not used -- LNA_TB.scs's self-contained flat subckt was used instead.

conversion.route: subckt body extracted by hand (cleaned_core.txt) -> parens stripped (spice2genie strip_parens=True, mirrors AnalogGenie's own read_netlist behaviour) -> spice2genie.convert() -> upstream graph/augmentation (execed read-only) -> token sequence -> lna/topology.py screen -> lna/to_spice.py -> ngspice
edits_from_source: Extracted only the device lines of subckt LNA_QM_V1 (R5 through R23) into cleaned_core.txt; the 'subckt'/'ends' wrapper lines and the enclosing testbench (V8/V6/V5/V3/C1/C0/PORT0/I0/analyses) were dropped -- AnalogGenie's format is topology-only and value-free, and the testbench is not part of the circuit under test.

DROPPED: L0 (net049 net048 VSS) ind 925pH. Its two non-ground nodes (net049, net048) do not appear on any other device line in this subckt excerpt, so within the file as retrieved L0 is a disconnected/orphan device -- structurally identical to the dataset's own index-1081 floating-inductor case documented in lna/WORKLOG.md R1. Since spice2genie.convert() hard-rejects disconnected graphs (by design, so a broken conversion never silently ships), and since I cannot infer what net049/net048 were meant to connect to elsewhere in the original (unretrieved) design hierarchy, I removed L0 rather than guess at connectivity. This is the ONLY device removed for connectivity reasons; every other device in the excerpt (including the 10-resistor VDD-to-output ladder network, whose exact function -- likely a gain-trim/tap network -- is not fully legible from this excerpt alone) was kept as found, on the principle of not editorially pruning real, connected topology just because its purpose is unclear.
No renaming was needed: element names already use plain SPICE letters (R#, C#, M#) with the '(pin list)' convention, which spice2genie handles once parentheses are stripped.

notes: Because L0 was the excerpt's only inductor, the converted circuit has zero inductors and 19 devices (over the structural screen's 15-device 'lna_sized' ceiling), so it is expected to score low on lna/topology.py's 5-point LNA screen (see convert_results.json) despite being a real, differential LNA core -- consistent with lna/FINDINGS.md's existing observation that inductorless/atypical real LNAs score under the screen's ceiling by design, not by screen error. Kept as ground truth anyway: a real, differential, resistively-loaded topology is a genuinely different archetype from the single-ended inductively-matched designs that dominate both the existing 41-circuit corpus and the two IHP siblings converted alongside this one. Unrelated to, and independent of, the Kanchetla et al. TMTT 2022 paper this pipeline is blind-reproducing.
